mainTopic: Whether טובת הנאה has monetary value, betrothal with מי חטאת and אפר פרה, and the opening משנה of the new פרק about a second man's betrothal
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story. רב הונא tells רבי חייא בר אבין 'הוצאה את', which embarrasses him, and then explains it was a compliment: רב אסי of הוצל agrees with him. The גמרא tries to show that whether טובת הנאה is worth money is a dispute between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about a thief who steals טבל. It rejects the proof several ways: unseparated gifts inherited from a grandfather who was a כהן, שמואל's rule that one grain exempts a pile, or a rabbinic penalty on the thief or on the owner. Next the גמרא asks how our משנה lets a man betroth with מי חטאת and אפר פרה, when a ברייתא says that taking pay for sprinkling makes them worthless. אביי answers that the משנה means pay for bringing and filling the water, and the wording of both sources supports him. The פרק הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ ends, and a new משנה teaches when a second man's betrothal takes effect and when the result is a doubt. The גמרא adds that an agent who betroths the woman for himself acted deceitfully, and it begins a question about the משנה's wording that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא's puzzling remark embarrasses רבי חייא בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says to רבי חייא בר אבין 'הוצאה את'. רבי חייא בר אבין is embarrassed because he thinks he is being told his הלכה is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'You are a הוצאה.' He was embarrassed, because he thought this was said about the הלכה he had stated.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a short story. רב הונא says something that sounds like 'you're out', and the listener takes it as a put-down of his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוצאה can sound like 'thrown out' or 'rejected'. So רבי חייא בר אבין understood that his ruling about טובת הנאה was being dismissed. The next step clears up the misunderstanding.

keyTerms.meaning: Sounds like 'out' or 'rejected', but can also mean someone from the town of הוצל
He was embarrassed
A halachic teaching or ruling

phrases.english: He said to him: You are 'out'.
phrases.notes: This is a play on words. It sounds like 'you're out', but it can also mean 'you're from הוצל'.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed,
for he thought: he is saying this to him because of the halacha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous part of the daf about רבי חייא בר אבין's ruling on טובת הנאה.

steps.title: רב הונא explains: רב אסי of הוצל agrees with you
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that he meant a compliment: רב אסי, who comes from הוצל, holds like רבי חייא בר אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I meant. רב אסי of הוצל stands with your opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא clears up the misunderstanding. 'הוצאה' was a nickname linking him to רב אסי of הוצל, who agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What sounded like a rejection was actually support. רבי חייא בר אבין's position is backed by another אמורא, רב אסי of הוצל. This closes the story before the גמרא moves on to look for a תנאים source.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I meant
A town, home of רב אסי
Stands with your view, agrees with you

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends on a positive note. רבי חייא בר אבין's ruling about טובת הנאה has the support of רב אסי of הוצל.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I meant:
Rav Asi of Huzal
stands in agreement with you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the misunderstood remark from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי of הוצל agrees with רבי חייא בר אבין.

steps.title: A dispute of תנאים about stealing טבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question may be a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about someone who steals his friend's טבל. רבי says he pays the full value of the טבל, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he pays only for the חולין part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים. One who steals his friend's טבל pays him the value of the טבל; these are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: he pays only the value of the חולין in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It brings a ברייתא with two opinions, and in the next step it will suggest that they argue about טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל contains portions that will become תרומה and מעשר, and those portions belong to a כהן or לוי, not to the owner. רבי makes the thief pay for everything. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him pay only for the part that truly belongs to the owner, the חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this matches a dispute of תנאים
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Ordinary, non-holy produce that belongs to the owner
One who steals

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
One who steals his friend's untithed produce

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם לוֹ דְּמֵי טִבְלוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: pays him the value of his friend's untithed produce,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶלָּא דְּמֵי חוּלִּין שֶׁבּוֹ.
phrases.english: He pays only the value of the non-sacred produce in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to searching for a תנאים source on טובת הנאה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether טובת הנאה ממון is already a dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה on stealing טבל

steps.title: Suggesting they argue whether the benefit of discretion is money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רבי holds טובת הנאה ממון, so the thief pays for everything, and that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds טובת הנאה אינה ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this? One master holds טובת הנאה is money, and the other holds טובת הנאה is not money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its proposed reading. The two תנאים are arguing exactly about whether טובת הנאה is worth money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of טבל cannot keep the תרומה and מעשר, but he does get to choose which כהן or לוי receives them. If that choice is worth money, the thief stole it too and must pay for it (רבי). If it is worthless, the thief pays only for the חולין (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה).

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that... (introduces a suggested reading)
The owner's benefit of choosing who receives his gifts
Money, monetary value
They disagree

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds: the benefit of discretion is money,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: the benefit of discretion is not money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from step 3 as a dispute about טובת הנאה.
steps.raayaObject: That טובת הנאה ממון is a תנאים dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinions of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in the ברייתא

steps.title: Rejection: the dispute is about inherited gifts not yet separated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Everyone agrees טובת הנאה אינה ממון. The case is a ישראל who inherited טבל from his mother's father, who was a כהן. They argue whether gifts that were never separated count as if they had been separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees טובת הנאה is not money. Here the case is טבל that came to him from his mother's father, a כהן, and they argue whether unseparated gifts are considered as if they were separated. One master holds they are considered separated, and the other holds they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It explains the ברייתא in a way that has nothing to do with טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandfather was a כהן, so the תרומה inside the טבל was his. Since the grandson is the child of a daughter, he is a ישראל, not a כהן. If unseparated gifts count as already separated, the grandson inherited the תרומה itself, and the thief must pay for it too (רבי). If they do not count as separated, he has only regular טבל with worthless טובת הנאה, so the thief pays only for the חולין (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה).

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
His mother's father
Gifts (תרומה and מעשר) that have not yet been separated
They are considered as if already separated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this means the grandson is a כהן. He comes from his mother's father, so he is a ישראל. That is why the question is whether he inherited the כהן's portions.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
the benefit of discretion is not money,
and here it is about untithed produce that came to him
from the house of his mother's father, a priest,
phrases.notes: His grandfather was a כהן, but he is not, because he descends through his mother.

phrases.english: and regarding gifts that were not separated,
whether they are considered as if separated, they disagree.
One master holds: they are considered as if separated.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָאו כְּמִי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ דָּמְיָין.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: they are not considered as if separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in step 4 by placing the ברייתא in a special case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא shows a dispute over טובת הנאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be explained as a dispute over whether unseparated gifts count as separated, in a case of inheritance from a grandfather who was a כהן.

steps.title: Second rejection: the dispute hinges on שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: everyone agrees that unseparated gifts count as separated and that טובת הנאה אינה ממון. They argue about the ruling of שמואל that one grain of wheat exempts a whole pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: everyone agrees they are considered as if separated, and טובת הנאה is not money. Here they argue about שמואל's ruling, as שמואל said: one grain of wheat exempts the pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to reject the proof. The dispute rests on the ruling of שמואל, and the גמרא will explain the connection next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the case is regular טבל, and both earlier questions are agreed upon. The new idea is שמואל's teaching that, by Torah law, giving even one grain as תרומה is enough for the whole pile. The next step explains how this leads to the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
One grain of wheat
Exempts
A pile of grain

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone agrees they are considered as if separated
and the benefit of discretion is not money,
and here they disagree about Shmuel's ruling.
As Shmuel said:
One grain of wheat exempts the whole pile.
phrases.notes: By Torah law, giving even a single grain as תרומה is enough to cover the whole pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּמִי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way, different from step 5, to reject the proof in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Again rejects the claim that the ברייתא is about טובת הנאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can depend on the ruling of שמואל about one grain exempting the pile, with no disagreement about טובת הנאה.

steps.title: One side holds like שמואל and the other does not
steps.stepSummary: This line completes the answer from Step 6: רבי holds like שמואל, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds like שמואל, and the other Sage does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in Step 6 by saying which side holds like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds like שמואל: the owner could have separated one grain as תרומה for the whole pile, so nearly all of it counts as his own, and the thief pays full value. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not hold like שמואל, so a real share counts as תרומה, and the thief pays only for the חולין part. Either way, the dispute has nothing to do with טובת הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'master'; here it means 'one Sage'
He holds (this view)
He does not hold (this view)

phrases.english: As one Sage holds of the ruling of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: שמואל's ruling is that a single grain can serve as תרומה for a whole pile.

phrases.english: and one Sage does not hold of the ruling of Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the alternative explanation begun in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Keeps the ברייתא from serving as proof about טובת הנאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained by שמואל's ruling instead of by טובת הנאה

steps.title: Everyone rejects שמואל, and רבי penalizes the thief
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation: nobody holds like שמואל. רבי makes the thief pay for everything as a penalty the Rabbis placed on thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: everyone disagrees with שמואל. רבי's reason here is that the Rabbis fined the thief.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read the dispute, again without any connection to טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By strict law the thief would not pay for the תרומה part, since טובת הנאה is not money. רבי still makes him pay full value because the Rabbis penalized him. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה simply does not apply this penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another explanation)
Everyone; all opinions agree
The Rabbis penalized him (a rabbinic fine)
Thief

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone does not hold of the ruling of Shmuel,
and here, this is the reason of Rabbi:
that the Rabbis penalized the thief.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new alternative rejection of the proof in Step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי holds טובת הנאה ממון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's ruling may come from a penalty on the thief, not from טובת הנאה being money

steps.title: Everyone accepts שמואל, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה penalizes the owner
steps.stepSummary: A last explanation: everyone holds like שמואל. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives the owner less as a penalty, because he should not have left his produce as טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: everyone agrees with שמואל. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reason is that the Rabbis fined the owner, because he should not have left his טבל lying around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more explanation. This time the penalty falls on the owner instead of the thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following שמואל, the owner should really get almost full value. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives him only the חולין value as a penalty for delaying the separation of his gifts. Again, the dispute does not depend on טובת הנאה, so the proof from Step 4 falls.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (here, the owner of the stolen produce)
To delay, to leave it waiting
His טבל, produce whose gifts were not yet separated

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about stolen טבל cannot prove anything about טובת הנאה. It can be explained by unseparated gifts, by שמואל's one-grain ruling, or by a penalty on the thief or on the owner.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone holds of the ruling of Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and here, this is the reason of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda:
that the Rabbis penalized the owner,
since he should not have delayed his untithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel alternative to Step 8, with the penalty now on the owner
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds טובת הנאה אינה ממון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His ruling may come from a penalty on the owner, not from the value of טובת הנאה

steps.title: Our משנה: betrothal with priestly gifts and purifying items works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a man who betroths with תרומות, מעשרות, priestly gifts, מי חטאת or אפר פרה succeeds, even if he is a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if a man betroths a woman with תרומות, מעשרות, priestly gifts, purifying water or red heifer ashes, she is betrothed, even if he is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה as a starting point. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats all these items as having enough value to make a betrothal work. That includes מי חטאת and אפר פרה. This is the point the next ברייתא will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
The gifts given to כהנים
The water used for purification together with the red heifer's ashes
The ashes of the red heifer
Betrothed

phrases.english: We learned: One who betroths with terumot,
or with tithes, or with the priestly gifts,
with the water of purification, or with the ashes of the heifer,
she is betrothed,
and even if he is an Israelite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the stolen טבל discussion back to our משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal with תרומות, מעשרות, priestly gifts, מי חטאת and אפר פרה works, even by a ישראל

steps.title: Contradiction: payment for sprinkling makes the water worthless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. Anyone who takes payment to judge, to testify, or to sprinkle or prepare the purifying water ruins what he does: his water is like cave water and his ashes are like ordinary burnt ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contradicted it from a ברייתא: one who takes pay to judge, his rulings are void. One who takes pay to testify, his testimony is void. One who takes pay to sprinkle or to prepare the purifying water, his water is just cave water and his ashes are just burnt ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says you may not take payment for sprinkling or preparing the purifying water; if you do, the water and ashes become worthless. Betrothing a woman with them is like getting paid for them. So how can the משנה say the betrothal works?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it (sets one source against another)
To sprinkle the purifying water on someone impure
Cave water, plain water with no purifying power
Ordinary ashes from burning, with no holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say these items lose their holiness by themselves. It is talking only about someone who takes payment for the service. The challenge is that using them for betrothal looks like taking payment.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who takes payment to judge, his judgments are void;
to testify, his testimony is void;
to sprinkle or to sanctify,
phrases.notes: To sanctify means putting the red heifer's ashes into the water to make it purifying water.

phrases.english: his water is cave water,
and his ashes are burnt ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that betrothal with מי חטאת and אפר פרה works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Payment for sprinkling or preparing the water makes it worthless. Betrothing with it is like taking payment, so the betrothal should fail.

steps.title: אביי: Bringing and Filling Versus Sprinkling and Mixing
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction. The משנה speaks about pay for bringing and filling the water, which is allowed. The ברייתא speaks about pay for sprinkling and mixing, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no contradiction. Here, in the משנה, it is about the pay for bringing the water and filling it. There, in the ברייתא, it is about the pay for sprinkling and for mixing the ashes into the water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 11 by showing that the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of the work with the פרה אדומה water may be paid, and some may not. Bringing the water and filling the vessel is ordinary labor, so its value can serve as קידושין. Sprinkling and mixing (קידוש) are the מצוה acts themselves, and taking pay for those ruins the water and ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difficulty. The usual way to start an answer to a contradiction.
Bringing the water and filling the vessel with it.
Sprinkling the purifying water on a person who is טמא.
Here it means mixing the פרה אדומה ashes into the water. It does not mean betrothal.

steps.confusionAlert: In this line, the word קִידּוּשׁ does not mean betrothal. It means putting the ashes into the water to make the purifying mixture.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult;
here it is with the pay for bringing and filling,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה: he betroths her with pay for bringing and filling the water, work you're allowed to be paid for.

phrases.english: there it is with pay for sprinkling and sanctifying.
phrases.notes: "There" is the ברייתא from Step 11. "Sanctifying" here means mixing the ashes into the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks about a different kind of work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה allows betrothing with the value of the very acts the ברייתא forbids being paid for.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about bringing and filling, which may be paid. The ברייתא speaks about sprinkling and mixing, which may not.

steps.title: The Wording of Both Sources Supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the exact words of the משנה and the ברייתא fit אביי's answer, and accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact. Here, in the משנה, it says "with מי חטאת and with אפר פרה," meaning the materials themselves. There, in the ברייתא, it says "to sprinkle and to sanctify," meaning the acts. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי by pointing to the precise words each source uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names objects: the water and the ash. This points to the stage before they are mixed, the bringing and filling. The ברייתא names actions: sprinkling and sanctifying. So each source really is talking about a different stage, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, meaning it supports the answer just given.
The purifying water used with the פרה אדומה ashes.
The ashes of the פרה אדומה.
Learn from it. The גמרא accepts the point as proven.

steps.whatToRemember: A person may betroth a woman with the value of the paid work of bringing and filling the purifying water. Pay for sprinkling or mixing is forbidden, and taking it ruins the water and ashes.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
for it teaches here: "With purification water and with heifer ash,"
and it teaches there: "To sprinkle and to sanctify."
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from Step 12 with proof from the wording.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split between bringing and filling versus sprinkling and mixing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה ("מי חטאת, אפר פרה") compared with the wording of the ברייתא ("להזות ולקדש").

steps.title: Hadran: Closing the Chapter הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the second פרק of קידושין, הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, "הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ."
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק has ended, and this is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no new argument here. The line marks the end of the פרק and shows our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The formula said when finishing a פרק.
"A man betroths." The name of the פרק, taken from its first words.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "A man betroths"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last סוגיא ends in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: The Second Man's Betrothal Takes Effect
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with two cases where the second man's קידושין works: an agent who betroths the woman for himself, and a man who betroths her during another man's 30-day delay. It adds that a בת ישראל betrothed to a כהן may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone tells his friend, "Go and betroth that woman for me," and the friend goes and betroths her for himself, she is betrothed to the second man, the friend. Similarly, if a man tells a woman, "You are betrothed to me after thirty days," and another man comes and betroths her within the thirty days, she is betrothed to the second man. A בת ישראל betrothed to a כהן may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins the next פרק. It gives cases where a second man's betrothal takes effect even though someone else had planned to marry the woman first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the שליח was only sent to act. His own betrothal is real, even if he acted wrongly. In the second case, the first man's betrothal has not started yet during the 30 days, so she is still free and the second man's betrothal takes hold. The line about תרומה shows that this is a full betrothal to the second man: if she is a בת ישראל and he is a כהן, she may already eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who says to his friend. Here he is appointing a שליח.
Go and betroth for me. These words make the friend his agent.
After thirty days. A betrothal set to take effect later.
She is betrothed to the second man.
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן and his household may eat.

steps.confusionAlert: "The second" in the first case means the agent, the friend who was sent. He is "second" because the first man is the one who sent him.

phrases.english: One who says to his friend:
"Go and betroth so-and-so woman to me,"
and he went and betrothed her to himself,
she is betrothed to the second.
phrases.notes: "The second" is the friend who was sent, not the man who sent him.

phrases.english: And similarly, one who says to a woman:

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם״
phrases.english: "You are hereby betrothed to me after thirty days,"

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא אַחֵר וְקִידְּשָׁהּ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם –
phrases.english: and another came and betrothed her within thirty days,
she is betrothed to the second.
An Israelite woman betrothed to a priest
may eat teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ: צֵא וְקַדֵּשׁ לִי אִשָּׁה פְּלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an agent betroths the woman for himself, or another man betroths her during a 30-day delay, she is fully betrothed to the second man. So if he is a כהן and she is a בת ישראל, she may eat תרומה.

steps.title: The 'from now and after 30 days' case is a doubt
steps.stepSummary: If the first man said 'from now and after 30 days' and a second man betrothed her within the 30 days, her status is a doubt. So she may not eat תרומה, whether a בת ישראל married a כהן or a בת כהן married a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'You are betrothed to me from now and after thirty days,' and another man came and betrothed her within the thirty days, she is betrothed and not betrothed. So if she is a ישראל's daughter betrothed to a כהן, or a כהן's daughter betrothed to a ישראל, she may not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a third case. The first man's wording is unclear, so we don't know whose wife she is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From now' suggests the first קידושין starts right away. 'After thirty days' suggests it only starts later. Because we can't decide, both men's קידושין are in doubt. So a בת ישראל can't eat תרומה as a כהן's wife, and a בת כהן loses her right to eat תרומה in her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: From now and after thirty days: the unclear wording that creates the doubt
Betrothed and not betrothed: her status is a doubt
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
A כהן's daughter, who may eat תרומה while she is in her father's house

steps.whatToRemember: There are three cases in this משנה. An agent who takes her for himself: the second man's קידושין works. 'After 30 days': the second man's קידושין works. 'From now and after 30 days': it is a doubt, so no תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the previous case. There, with plain 'after 30 days,' she is fully betrothed to the second man, so if he is a כהן she may eat תרומה. Here the added word 'from now' makes her status a doubt, so she may not.

phrases.english: 'From now and after thirty days'
phrases.notes: These are the first man's words to the woman: 'You are betrothed to me from now and after thirty days.'

phrases.english: and another man came and betrothed her
within the thirty days –
she is betrothed and not betrothed.
phrases.notes: It's a doubt, not that she's half-married. We don't know which man's קידושין took hold.

phrases.english: A ישראל's daughter betrothed to a כהן,
or a כהן's daughter betrothed to a ישראל –
may not eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 15, adding a third case whose result is a doubt instead of a clear ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'from now and after 30 days,' if a second man betroths her within the 30 days, her קידושין is doubtful, so she may not eat תרומה.

steps.title: The agent's קידושין works, but he acted deceitfully
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins on the משנה's first case, an agent who betroths the woman for himself. A ברייתא teaches that his קידושין is valid, but he behaved deceitfully toward the man who sent him.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About 'one who says to his friend, Go and betroth for me': a תנא taught: What he did is done, but he acted toward him in a deceitful way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה's first case. It brings a ברייתא that adds a moral point the משנה did not state outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gave the legal result: the woman is betrothed to the agent. The ברייתא adds that this result does not make his behavior right. He tricked the man who trusted him, and that is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Go and betroth: sending someone as an agent to betroth a woman for you
A ברייתא taught (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
What he did is done: the act is legally valid
Deceit, trickery

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea in הלכה: an act can work legally and still be forbidden to do.

phrases.english: גמרא: 'One who says to his friend: Go and betroth.'
A תנא taught: What he did is done,
but he treated him in a deceitful way.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man who sent the agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the first case of the משנה (from step 15).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The agent's קידושין for himself is valid, but he acted deceitfully.

steps.title: Our משנה hints at the deceit with the word 'went'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה's word 'הָלַךְ' (he went) hints at the same point: he went with trickery.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא too, when he says 'went,' means he went deceitfully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that our משנה agrees with the ברייתא. It finds the hint in one extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could simply have said 'and he betrothed her for himself.' The extra word 'הָלַךְ' looks unneeded, so it must be teaching something: that he went off and acted deceitfully. So the משנה and the ברייתא do not disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא: the author of our משנה
He went: the word in the משנה used for the hint
That he teaches / says

phrases.english: And our תנא,
when he also says 'went' –
phrases.notes: The משנה says 'and he went and betrothed her for himself.' The word 'went' seems extra.

phrases.english: means he went with deceit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא's point (step 17) is already hinted at in the wording of our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה also holds the agent acted deceitfully.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra word 'הָלַךְ' in the משנה.

steps.title: Why is this case worded 'one who says to his friend'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new question about the משנה's wording: why does it open this case with 'הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ'? The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here, that it says 'one who says to his friend'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question about how the משנה words this case. The rest of the question and the answer come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is about to compare this wording with how a similar case is worded elsewhere. It wants to know why the משנה chose 'הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ' here. For now, just notice the focus: why this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different: a phrase that opens a comparison question
Here

phrases.english: What is different here,
that it teaches 'one who says to his friend,'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָתָנֵי הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the deceit point to a new question about the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה words this case as 'הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ' (the comparison continues on the next amud).
